page: Amazon Web Services c9g.medium is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro Hypervisor. It features a single dedicated arm64 vCPU powered by an AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 2.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Cache hardware includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. It features no local ephemeral SSD storage and relies on external storage volumes, while delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong single-threaded processing capabilities along with constrained memory subsystem throughput. In single-threaded compression evaluations, the instance achieves 36.12 GB/sec in gzip compression and 16.83 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, placing its decompression performance in the upper tier. Due to its single physical core constraint, multi-core stress-ng performance scores at 1991.89 and Passmark CPU benchmarks reach 1423.8. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 38.46 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 13.36 GB/sec.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, c9g.medium provides an entry point for ARMv9 execution without carrying costs for unneeded memory or local storage overhead. The hardware profile is appropriate for lightweight microservices, single-threaded batch processing, small utility scripts, and low-traffic static web serving workloads requiring predictable dedicated CPU allocation.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.medium is a compute-optimized instance utilizing the AWS Nitro Hypervisor and an ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 Graviton processor running at 3.3 GHz. It is configured with 1 dedicated physical vCPU, 2.0 GB of RAM, a 48 MB L3 cache, and a 1 Gbps baseline network connection, with no local ephemeral storage or integrated GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate notable strength in single-threaded decompression and compression, recording 16.83 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression and 36.12 GB/sec in gzip compression. Conversely, its single-core ceiling limits overall multi-core throughput, yielding a Passmark CPU score of 1423.8 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 38.46 GB/sec. Application tests register 3.3 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.13 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Economical for minimal compute footprints, the instance provides cost-effective dedicated single-core processing. It is suited for single-threaded batch processing, lightweight microservices, utility scripting, and low-traffic web serving.
